summary.headline: ABD Q2 FY27 income from operations rose 15.8% YoY to ₹1,152 crore and volumes crossed 10 million cases for the first time, while reported EBITDA margin fell to 12.4%.
summary.overview: Consolidated income from operations was ₹1,152 crore, up 15.8% YoY and 17.1% QoQ, with volumes of 10 million cases (up 11.1% YoY). Reported gross margin was 45.3% (up 90 bps YoY), but global supply chain disruptions cost ₹29 crore in the quarter, so reported EBITDA of ₹143 crore (12.4% margin, down 66 bps YoY) and PAT of ₹69 crore understate underlying performance. Mass Premium & Others drove growth, with Prestige & Above volume growth slowing to 6.1% YoY. Net debt rose to ₹1,273 crore, pushing Net Debt/EBITDA to 2.2x, marginally above the 2.0x framework.

financial_highlights.change: +11.1% YoY (9.0 mn cases in Q2 FY26)
+90 bps YoY; 47.9% excluding ₹29 crore supply chain impact (+342 bps YoY)
EBITDA +5.8% YoY; PAT vs ₹119 crore in H1 FY26
up ₹292 crore from ₹981 crore at Mar 2026; Net Debt/EBITDA 2.2x, Net Debt/Equity 0.8x

segments.name: Mass Premium & Others
segments.commentary: Net sales ₹468 crore (+15.9% YoY, +21.1% QoQ); volume 5.5 million cases (+15.5% YoY); realisation ₹848/case (+0.4% YoY). Growth led by brandy in Andhra Pradesh and a recovery in Officer's Choice Whisky.

segments.name: Prestige & Above
segments.commentary: Sales ₹605 crore (+13.4% YoY, +7.5% QoQ); volume 4.5 million cases (+6.1% YoY); realisation ₹1,339/case (+6.9% YoY). Share of value 56.4% (vs 56.9%) and of volume 45.0% (vs 47.1%).

segments.name: ICONiQ White
segments.commentary: 3.2 million cases in Q2 FY27 (+20.6% YoY from 2.6 mn); H1 FY27 at 6.2 million cases (+26.8% YoY). FY27 target about 14 million cases (FY26: 10.7 million).

segments.name: ABD Maestro (super-premium to luxury)
segments.commentary: FY26 sales about ₹40 crore; FY27 target about ₹80 crore. Present in about 80% of addressable markets in India, 7 export countries, and 6,000 premium touchpoints at FY26 exit.

guidance_outlook: Topline expected to grow in line with the stated guidance of mid-teens for FY27.
FY27 EBITDA margin guided broadly in line with FY26; management says the West Asia-related disruption cost about 250 bps of margin, and it expects to match FY26 margin by FY27 close.
H2 FY27 gross margin expected to gain about 100 bps from seasonality and premium mix (vs 46% in Q1 and 45.3% in Q2).
Backward integration expected to add about 300 bps EBITDA margin by FY28 and a further 150 bps in FY29 (management also cited 400-450 bps cumulative by FY29 in one answer).
ICONiQ White target of about 14 million cases in FY27; management aspires to 20 million cases within two years.
Net Debt/EBITDA and Net Debt/Equity expected to return within the 2.0x and 0.75x frameworks on a full-year basis.
Export footprint target of 50-plus countries within 12 months (42 at Q2 FY27).
capex_capacity: Total capex programme about ₹1,600 crore; about 25% spent through FY26, about ₹300 crore spent in FY27 so far, balance over the next 3 years. Management sees no capex beyond this other than maintenance.
Maintenance capex estimated at ₹75-100 crore per year across 40 manufacturing plants.
Rangapur, Telangana: captive malt distillery commissioned in October 2026, about ₹75 crore investment, 4.0 million bulk litres per year. PET bottle plant (commissioned FY26) is EBITDA accretive.

Minakshi Agro (Aurangabad, Maharashtra): bottling unit expected operational in the next couple of months; ENA distillery expansion has environment clearance, construction under way, targeted for H1 FY28.

Uttar Pradesh (Moradabad): bottling facility commenced commercial operations in October 2026 with 6 million cases per year initial capacity; plan to expand to 13 million cases by Q3 FY28. New 66 million bulk litre per year dual-mode distillery announced August 2026 at about ₹293.5 crore; separate ~₹202 crore for bottling expansion, molasses refurbishment and land; overall UP investment above ₹600 crore.
demand_pricing: Volume growth was broad-based across Mass Premium & Others and Prestige & Above; all four millionaire brands grew sequentially. Record monthly volume above 3.5 million cases in September 2026.
Officer's Choice Blue refreshed packaging launched September 2026 in UP, Maharashtra, Haryana and West Bengal; management reports quarter-on-quarter growth in Q2 after YoY declines moderated.
The Indian Edit launched September 2026 in 7 states, priced around ₹1,550 in Maharashtra per an analyst question.

Karnataka: market about 65 million cases a year; ABD holds about 40,000-50,000 cases a month; premium is 10-12% of market; sub-premium brands cut prices by lowering alcohol strength. ICONiQ growth seen over the last 2 months.
Tamil Nadu (over 50 lakh cases a month) seen as opening up, with new brands being registered; management expects value and margin accretion.
Pricing: management is lobbying for price increases in Telangana and other states; no quantified price increase given.
India-UK FTA: management expects about 70 bps margin benefit this year, but uncertainty over bulk scotch import duty under applicable HSN codes; stocks last until early December.

qa_highlights.question: Why did ICONiQ White volume grow only marginally QoQ (3.1 mn in Q1 to 3.2 mn in Q2), and is it maturing?
qa_highlights.answer: Management called Q1 an aberration; FY27 target is about 14 million cases (over 25% growth), and the brand has exceeded 1 million cases a month since April.

qa_highlights.question: Will further capex be announced beyond the current programme, and what is maintenance capex?
qa_highlights.answer: Current programme is about ₹1,600 crore, of which 25% spent through FY26; no further capex beyond this apart from maintenance of ₹75-100 crore a year.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Prestige & Above growth (about 6%) lag Mass Premium (about 15%), and how will P&A recover?
qa_highlights.answer: P&A volume grew 6% but value 13.4%; Mass Premium's revival diluted P&A salience. Management targets 50%+ volume and 60%+ value saliency within a year, with ICONiQ seasonally weighted to H2 and an OC Blue and Sterling Reserve reset planned, plus a vodka launch before year-end.

qa_highlights.question: How should gross margin progress in H2 given the supply chain impact and UK FTA benefits?
qa_highlights.answer: Market seasonality should add about 100 bps to gross margin in H2; backward integration benefits are expected in FY28-FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Is ICONiQ cannibalising the other brands, and what is being done on OC Blue and Sterling Reserve B7?
qa_highlights.answer: Management denied cannibalisation, citing ICONiQ at more than 1 million cases a month; SR B7 packaging roll-out is targeted for Q4 FY27.

qa_highlights.question: How is the company funding capex with leverage above the framework?
qa_highlights.answer: H1 FY27 operating cash flow was ₹269 crore (vs ₹147 crore); management expects metrics to fall within the framework by year-end.

qa_highlights.question: What is the pricing strategy given cost inflation and how much margin is lost to the West Asia conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is lobbying states (Telangana the main near-term case) for price increases; it estimates the West Asia-linked inflation cost about 250 bps of EBITDA margin and expects it to be temporary.

risks_watch: Gross margin pressure from global supply chain disruption (₹29 crore in Q2, ₹53 crore in H1); management says inflationary pressure persists and Q4 should be better.
Net Debt/EBITDA of 2.2x and Net Debt/Equity of 0.8x are above framework; full-year compliance depends on capex timing and cash generation.
ICONiQ White must grow about 30% in H2 to reach 14 million cases, with Q2 volume only marginally above Q1; Karnataka competitive changes are unresolved.
Prestige & Above volume growth of 6% and declining share of P&A volume; OC Blue and SR B7 recovery depends on packaging resets due H2 and Q4 FY27.
India-UK FTA bulk scotch duty uncertainty; management expects resolution within about a month, with stock cover to early December.
Telangana price revision and dues clearance still pending.
key_quotes: So, I have lost about 250 basis points of EBITDA margin because of the West Asia crisis.
This is just an aberration. The plan for ICONiQ during the current year is to reach a level of close to 14 million cases, which is in excess of 25% growth by the year-end.
So, we are not scared of competition, but we will just concentrate on elevating our position in the market over the next 2 years.
But right now, the pressure is on.
I think we have no doubt that the financial metrics that we talk about as per our stated guidelines by the end of the year when the capex program starts justifying, we will fall in line.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume momentum, ICONiQ White and the backward integration roadmap, but cautious on near-term margins, citing West Asia-linked inflation and supply chain costs. Management was evasive on Q3 trends, the pace of Telangana price revisions and the India-UK FTA bulk scotch duty, and it deflected the cannibalisation question.
